### Pipeline

All analyses were performed with a workflow implemented in Nextflow DSL2 [@ditommaso2017]. Each library was downloaded, quality-filtered and screened for papillomavirus reads, and the HPV-positive libraries were then aligned to an HPV reference panel for typing and for classification of early and late viral transcripts. The tools, versions and thresholds used at each step are listed in @supptbl-pipeline. The reference panel comprised `r stats$panel_n` complete HPV genomes from PaVE [@vandoorslaer2017] and NCBI RefSeq, covering the alpha, beta, gamma, mu and nu genera. Because both sources are updated continuously, the panel was fixed at its build date of 17 April 2026. Reads were not subsampled at any step: the reads reaching the Kraken2 screen were a median `r pp(stats$spot_med)`% of the spot count reported by the SRA, and between `r pp(stats$spot_tier_lo)`% and `r pp(stats$spot_tier_hi)`% in the individual sample groups.

::: {#supptbl-pipeline}

| Step | Tool (version) | Settings and thresholds |
|:---|:---|:------|
| Reference panel | PaVE 2.0, RefSeq; seqkit ≥ 2.5 [@shen2016] | Genomes deduplicated by identifier; gene models for E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7, L1 and L2 from the PaVE annotation |
| Download | SRA Toolkit 3.1.1 [@leinonen2011] | `prefetch`, then `fasterq-dump --split-3` with no spot limit |
| Read QC | fastp 0.23.4 [@chen2018] | Base quality ≥ Phred 20; minimum read length 36 nt |
| HPV screen | Kraken2 ≥ 2.1.3 [@wood2019] | Database of GRCh38 plus the panel; HPV-positive at ≥ 10 Papillomaviridae reads |
| Alignment | STAR 2.7.11b [@dobin2013] | End-to-end, unspliced, ≤ 3 mismatches, ≤ 50 multi-mapping loci |
| Typing | samtools 1.21 [@danecek2021] | MAPQ ≥ 10; type assigned at coverage breadth ≥ 0.10 and mean depth ≥ 2 |
| Transcript classes | featureCounts ≥ 2.0 [@liao2014] | Overlap ≥ 20 nt, MAPQ ≥ 10; early = E1 to E7, late = L1 and L2; productive at ≥ 3 L1 reads |
| Burden | Kraken2 report | RPM = Papillomaviridae reads / (unclassified + root reads) × 10⁶ |

Alignment, typing and transcript classification were applied to HPV-positive libraries only, whereas burden was scored for every screened library, including HPV-negative ones.

**Pipeline steps, tools and thresholds.**
:::

### Cohort and sample groups

Public human RNA-seq runs were identified by Entrez queries of the Sequence Read Archive (SRA), each of which was intersected with the filter `"Homo sapiens"[Organism] AND "RNA-Seq"[Strategy] AND "public"[Access]`. Three queries were used: an untargeted sweep of skin and related tissues, a targeted query for productive lesions (epidermodysplasia verruciformis, warts and condyloma), and a query for cutaneous neoplasia (cSCC, actinic keratosis and Bowen disease). For each run, the tissue site, the diagnosis, and the cell-line, engineered and in-vitro status were assigned by keyword matching of the SRA metadata. These annotations were used to classify libraries, not to exclude them, and the annotations of the untargeted sweep were additionally refined by manual curation. On the basis of these annotations, each library was assigned to one of eight mutually exclusive sample groups. Seven groups were assigned from the metadata in a fixed order of precedence: `cell_line` (*n* = `r comma(stats$cl2_n)`), `engineered` (`r comma(stats$engt_n)`), `EV` (`r comma(stats$ev_n)`), `control_productive` (warts and condyloma; `r comma(stats$ctrl_n)`), `neoplasia` (`r comma(stats$neo_n)`), `unselected_skin` (`r comma(stats$uns_n)`) and `other` (`r comma(stats$oth_n)`; shown as "Site not recorded" in the figures and tables). The eighth group, `non_permissive_tissue` (`r comma(stats$npt_n)`), consists of adipose tissue, blood cells and neural cells. Because this group cannot be recognized from a diagnosis field, it was assigned study by study.

### Studies not used as non-permissive controls

Two studies that include tissue which cannot host HPV were not assigned to `non_permissive_tissue`, because their HPV signal far exceeded that of the other non-permissive studies, in which `r pp(stats$npt_pctany)`% of libraries carried an any-HPV read and no library exceeded `r formatC(stats$npt_max, format = "f", digits = 2)` RPM. In SRP572742 (skeletal muscle, blood and skin from patients with myotonic dystrophy), `r round(stats$ho1_non$pct)`% of the `r stats$ho1_non$n` muscle and blood libraries carried an any-HPV read, with a maximum of `r p1(stats$ho1_non$max)` RPM. In SRP565659, a study of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma in which skin and blood of the same patients were sequenced together, an any-HPV read was carried by `r round(stats$ho2_skin$pct)`% of the `r stats$ho2_skin$n` skin libraries (maximum `r p1(stats$ho2_skin$max)` RPM) and by `r round(stats$ho2_non$pct)`% of the `r stats$ho2_non$n` blood and lymph-node libraries (maximum `r p1(stats$ho2_non$max)` RPM). No library of either study reached the detection floor. Because neither muscle nor blood contains stratified squamous epithelium, the signal in these libraries was attributed to carry-over between libraries that were sequenced together and not to infection. The `r stats$ho_non_n` non-skin libraries of the two studies were left in `other`, and their `r stats$ho_skin_n` skin libraries remained in `unselected_skin`.

Because this decision selects the non-permissive group on the outcome that the group is meant to measure, we also report the comparison without it. With the `r stats$ho_non_n` non-skin libraries included, the any-HPV rate of non-permissive tissue was `r pp(stats$npp_pct)`% (`r stats$npp_k` of `r stats$npp_n`). Non-permissive libraries were also sequenced more deeply than unselected-skin libraries (median `r mreads(stats$npt_medM)` against `r mreads(stats$uns_medM)` reads), and the any-HPV rate rises with depth. In a logistic regression with log~10~ library size as a covariate, the odds of an any-HPV read in unselected skin relative to non-permissive tissue were `r fo(stats$bg_adj$OR)` (95% CI `r oci(stats$bg_adj$lo, stats$bg_adj$hi)`; *P* = `r fp(stats$bg_adj$p)`) with the two studies held out and `r fo(stats$bg_adj_pool$OR)` (95% CI `r oci(stats$bg_adj_pool$lo, stats$bg_adj_pool$hi)`; *P* = `r fp(stats$bg_adj_pool$p)`) with them included. Under either treatment, the any-HPV rate of unselected skin is of the same order as that of tissue that cannot be infected.

### Metadata corrections

Studies submitted with incomplete or misleading metadata were corrected through a curated override table (`assets/tier_overrides.csv`). In total, the override table reassigned `r comma(stats$ovr_moved)` of the `r comma(stats$ovr_before)` libraries for which RPM was measured. Most of these reassignments concerned studies whose metadata contain no usable annotation of site or tissue. First, `r comma(stats$ovr_site_n)` libraries from `r stats$ovr_site_studies` studies carried no site keyword, although the study records identify the material as skin; these libraries were moved from `other` to `unselected_skin`. Of these libraries, `r pp(stats$site_pctany)`% carried an any-HPV read and `r if (stats$site_floor == 0) "none" else stats$site_floor` reached the detection floor; without them, unselected skin comprises `r comma(stats$nosite_n)` libraries, of which `r stats$nosite_floor` reach the floor and `r pp(stats$nosite_pctany)`% carry an any-HPV read. Second, the `r comma(stats$ovr_npt_n)` libraries of `non_permissive_tissue`, from `r stats$ovr_npt_studies` studies, were assigned through the same table. Third, `r stats$ovr_cellstudy_n` libraries from `r nword(stats$ovr_cellstudy_studies)` studies of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma lines, their xenografts or organotypic cultures, which had been deposited as tissue, were flagged as cell line; `r stats$ovr_cellstudy_neo` of them had been grouped as `neoplasia` and `r stats$ovr_cellstudy_uns` as `unselected_skin`. The remaining `r stats$ovr_other` reassignments were identified by inspecting every library that reached the detection floor. They comprise `r stats$ovr_ev` epidermodysplasia verruciformis skin biopsies [@saeidian2023] that were annotated only as skin and were reassigned to `EV`, `r nword(stats$ovr_cell)` HPV31-positive HaCaT libraries that carried no cell-line annotation and were flagged as cell line, and `r nword(stats$ovr_wart)` primary wart whose metadata held a sample label in the `cell_line` field and which was returned to `control_productive`. Because only libraries at or above the floor were inspected, these corrections can only lower the floor-level rate of the groups that the libraries left. The effect is small: `r stats$undo_n` of the `r stats$ovr_other` libraries had been grouped as unselected skin, and had they remained there, `r stats$undo_floor` of `r comma(stats$undo_tot)` unselected-skin libraries (`r formatC(stats$undo_pct, format = "f", digits = 2)`%) would have reached the floor instead of `r stats$uns_floor_n` of `r comma(stats$uns_n)` (`r formatC(stats$uns_floor_pct, format = "f", digits = 2)`%). The override table also specifies the `r comma(stats$ovr_excluded)` excluded libraries that are described in the next section.

### Unscreened and excluded libraries

The unscreened libraries of the untargeted sweep are described in the main Methods. Among the `r comma(stats$les_submitted)` targeted lesion libraries, `r stats$les_unscr` were unscreened because their reads were shorter than the 36 nt minimum. They fall into three classes of read geometry: `r stats$les_unscr_pe_short` libraries from two spatial-profiling studies (SRP413119 and SRP413116), in which both mates are 27 to 28 nt long; `r stats$les_unscr_bc` libraries with the layout of droplet single-cell sequencing, in which a barcode read of 26 to 28 nt is paired with a cDNA read; and `r stats$les_unscr_se` single-end libraries of 35 nt. Of these `r stats$les_unscr` libraries, `r stats$les_unscr_dx` carried a diagnosis of carcinoma, condyloma or papilloma. All unscreened libraries are listed in Data S2 together with the reason for their loss. We excluded `r stats$excl_amplicon` 16S rRNA amplicon libraries that were retrieved by the query, and `r nword(stats$excl_animal)` libraries of a study that was deposited as human actinic keratosis but whose publication describes an animal experiment. We also excluded `r stats$excl_adjacent` libraries of mucosa adjacent to condyloma, obtained from 5 donors; in tissue so close to a productive lesion, an independent infection cannot be distinguished from signal originating in the lesion itself. After these exclusions, the burden analysis included `r comma(stats$n_burden)` libraries, of which `r comma(stats$n_both)` were also among the libraries screened in the untargeted sweep.

### Statistical analysis

The detection floor was defined as the 5th percentile of RPM among the productive controls that were not cell lines. HPV positivity was modeled by logistic regression on sample class, a three-level classification (clinical, engineered or cell-line material) of the `r comma(stats$n_screened)` libraries screened in the untargeted sweep. Any-HPV detection and detection at or above the floor were each modeled by logistic regression on sample group (neoplasia against unselected skin; `r comma(stats$m2_n)` libraries), with log~10~ library size included as a covariate. As a further control for sequencing depth, the fraction of libraries at or above the floor was compared between groups within matched depth bins (<5M, 5–10M, 10–20M, 20–40M and >40M reads). The productivity contrasts were evaluated with Fisher exact tests.

To assess the robustness of these results, the three models were refitted as Bayesian logistic regressions in rstanarm [@rstanarm]. Each model was run with four Markov chains of 2,000 iterations (all R-hat ≤ 1.004, no divergent transitions) and with weakly informative priors: Normal(0, 2.5) on the log-odds coefficients and Normal(0, 5) on the intercept. Because productive controls and unselected skin are almost completely separated, this contrast was additionally fitted under a heavier-tailed Student-*t*(3) prior (@supptbl-bayes).

### Library-selection chemistry

The library-selection chemistry of each library was obtained from the SRA `LibrarySelection` field. This field holds the uninformative value "cDNA" for `r pp(stats$chem_cdna_pct)`% of libraries. For these libraries, chemistry was instead inferred from the text of the library-construction protocol, which was matched against curated sets of phrases that indicate poly-A selection or rRNA depletion (`bin/classify_library_chemistry.py`). Droplet-based 3'-barcoded libraries and SMART template-switching libraries were coded as separate categories, because neither is a selection chemistry. A library was labeled as "unspecified" when its protocol text supported both chemistries or neither. With this procedure, chemistry was resolved for `r comma(stats$chem_n)` of `r comma(stats$chem_total)` libraries (`r pp(stats$chem_pct)`%).

### Integration status

Integration status was inferred from the ratio of E1 to E2 transcripts. Each library with at least 5 combined E1 and E2 reads was scored as log~2~((E1 + 0.5)/(E2 + 0.5)), and the scores of the sample groups were compared by the area under the ranked ratio and by the Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Single-cell and single-nucleus libraries were excluded from this analysis, because their 3'-biased coverage does not support a ratio across the early region.

The ratio was validated in two ways. The first validation used virus-host junctions in `r stats$jx_n` libraries that spanned the range of the ratio. The reads of these libraries were aligned with STAR to a combined index of GRCh38 and the HPV reference panel, with chimeric detection enabled (`--chimSegmentMin 20`, `--chimJunctionOverhangMin 15`). Integration was then scored as junction clustering, defined as the fraction of the virus-host junctions of a library that fall at its most frequently supported pair of coordinates. The observed values of junction clustering were bimodal, with no values between `r stats$jx_epi_range` and `r stats$jx_int_range`, and the threshold for integration was therefore set at 0.2.

The second validation used an independent graded cervical series of rRNA-depleted libraries (BioProject PRJNA612785), which comprises HPV16-positive normal epithelium, high-grade lesions and carcinoma, with six cases in each arm. These libraries were processed with the same workflow and thresholds as the skin cohort and were evaluated against the labels assigned by the original study. In the normal, high-grade lesion and carcinoma arms, `r stats$cxg_norm_n`, `r stats$cxg_hsil_n` and `r stats$cxg_scc_n` libraries, respectively, carried at least 5 viral gene reads, and `r stats$cxg_norm_nr`, `r stats$cxg_hsil_nr` and `r stats$cxg_scc_nr` of them had the 5 E1 and E2 reads that are required for a ratio (@fig-integration c).
